Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
ELECTRONIC PRINCIPLES AND DEVICES

Clampers


    • A clamper is a circuit with a diode, resistor, and
   capacitor that shifts a waveform to a new DC
   level without altering its shape.


   • Also known as DC restorer.

  •  Clamping networks have a capacitor connected
     directly from input                                                                      Fig.1: Clamper

  •  Resistive element connected in parallel with the
    output signal.

  • The diode is also in parallel with the output
     signal but may or may not have a series dc
    supply as an added element.

      25-09-2026                                                                                                                           3

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
ELECTRONIC PRINCIPLES AND DEVICES

  Steps used for analysis:


Step 1: Examine the response of the portion of the input
   signal that will forward bias the diode.
      • For Fig. 2, the diode is forward biased during the
        positive portion of the signal.
      • The short-circuit equivalent for the diode results in
     Vo = 0 V for t = 0 to T/2 .
Step 2: During the on period of the diode, assume that the
  capacitor will charge up instantaneously to a voltage                     Fig.2                                Fig.3
   level determined by the surrounding network.

Step 3: Assume the capacitor retains its voltage while the
diode is "off."
Step 4: Track the position and polarity of v o to ensure
correct levels.
• When the input turns negative, the network appears as
in Fig. 3, with the diode as an open circuit and voltage
stored across the capacitor.
Step 5: Check that the total swing of the output matches
   that of the input. (see Fig. 4)                                                                                                                         Fig. 4         25-09-2026                                                                                                                           4

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
ELECTRONIC PRINCIPLES AND DEVICES

   Numerical

Example1: Determine Vo for the network of shown below, for the input indicated in Fig. 1.1

   Solution:
   Note: f = 1000 Hz => time period, T= 1 ms
   Step 1: For t1→ t2 of the vi since the diode is in its short-
    circuit state. The network appears as shown in Fig. 1.2 .

   Step 2: The output is across R (also directly across the 5-V
                                                                                                  Fig. 1.1
   battery). So, v o = 5 V.
   Applying KVL around the input loop
   -20 V + VC - 5 V = 0
   and VC = 25 V  => the capacitor charges to 25 V.

   Step 3: For the period t2→t3 the network will appear as
   shown in Fig. 1.3 .                                                                                         Fig. 1.2 : Determining Vo                Fig. 1.3: Determining v o
   Applying KVL around the outside loop of the network                 and VC with the                      with the diode
   +10 V + 25 V - vo = 0                                                     diode in the “on” state.                    in the “off” state.
   vo = 35 V

            25-09-2026                                                                                                                           5

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
ELECTRONIC PRINCIPLES AND DEVICES

Numerical




 Step 4: The time constant of the network of Fig. 1.3 is
 determined by the product RC and has the magnitude
  ζ = RC = (100 kΩ)(0.1 μF) = 0.01 s = 10 ms

 The total discharge time is: 5 ζ = 5(10 ms) = 50 ms



 Step 5: The resulting output appears in Fig. 1.4 with the input                                                                                                   Fig. 1.4:  Input and Output Waveform
  signal.
  Note: The output swing of 30 V matches the input swing.





      25-09-2026                                                                                                                           6

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
ELECTRONIC PRINCIPLES AND DEVICES

   Numerical

Example 2: Repeat example 1, using a silicon diode with Vk = 0.7 V.

 Solution:

        For the short-circuit state, the network appears as in Fig. 2.1 , and v o
            is determined by KVL in the output section as:
       +5 V - 0.7 V - vo = 0
       and vo = 4.3 V

                                                                                                                             Fig.2.1
        For the input section, KVL results in
        -20 V + VC + 0.7 V - 5 V = 0
       and VC = 24.3 V

        For the period t2 →t3 the network will now appear as in Fig. 2.2 , with
        the only change being the voltage across the capacitor.
         Applying KVL yields
       +10 V + 24.3 V - vo = 0
       and vo = 34.3 V
                                                                                                                             Fig.2.2
